questions.question: What is an abstract class?
options: A class that cannot be inherited
A class that cannot be instantiated directly
explanations: Correct. Objects can only be created from its subclasses.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to implement an interface?
explanations: Correct. implements establishes that the class fulfills the contract.

questions.question: How many interfaces can a class implement?
explanations: Only one class can be extended.
Correct. Java allows implementing multiple interfaces.
It can implement none or several.
It does not depend on the version.

questions.question: What does an abstract method do?
options: It has no body; subclasses must implement it
explanations: Correct. abstract void doSomething(); → no body, mandatory to implement.

questions.question: When do you use interface vs abstract class?
options: Abstract: to share code. Interface: to define a contract
explanations: Correct. Abstract class for shared code, interface for a pure contract.

questions.question: Can an interface have attributes?
explanations: It can have attributes, but they are constants.
Correct. Attributes in interfaces are implicitly public static final.
